# Elucim

> Elucim is a React library for creating animated math and concept visualizations — 3Blue1Brown-style, built for the web. It provides SVG primitives, animation components, a frame-driven Player, slide Presentations, and a JSON/YAML DSL for AI-generated content.

## Packages

- `@elucim/core`: React components for animated visualizations — primitives, animations, Player, Presentation, hooks, easing, export
- `@elucim/dsl`: Normalized JSON/YAML document model, DslRenderer component, validator, agent operations, polish nudges, semantic layout, composite helpers, and themes for declarative/AI-generated content
- `@elucim/editor`: Visual editor for normalized Elucim documents
- `@elucim/cli`: Agent-friendly CLI for validating, inspecting, polishing, laying out, and adding composites to `.elc` documents

## Core Concepts

Elucim is frame-based. A `Player` defines `fps` and `durationInFrames`, wrapping a `Scene` SVG viewport. Components inside use `useCurrentFrame()` to read the current frame and `interpolate()` to map frame ranges to values. Document motion is represented by timeline tracks, reveal effects, and state machines.

## Components

### Playback
- `Player`: Interactive player with controls, scrubber, play/pause, keyboard shortcuts. Props: `width`, `height`, `fps`, `durationInFrames`, `controls`, `loop`, `autoPlay`, `background`
- `Scene`: Raw SVG scene (used internally by Player). Props: `width`, `height`, `background`

### Primitives
- `Circle`: SVG circle. Props: `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `stroke`, `fill`, `strokeWidth`
- `Rect`: Rectangle. Props: `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `rx`, `stroke`, `fill`
- `Line`: Line segment or straight connector. Props: `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `lineStyle`, `startCap`, `endCap`
- `BezierCurve`: Smooth connector/path. Props: `x1`, `y1`, `cx1`, `cy1`, `cx2`, `cy2`, `x2`, `y2`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `lineStyle`, `startCap`, `endCap`
- `Text`: SVG text. Props: `x`, `y`, `content`, `fill`, `fontSize`, `textAnchor`, `fontWeight`
- `Polygon`: Arbitrary polygon. Props: `points` (array of [x,y])

### Math Visualizations
- `Axes`: Coordinate axes. Props: `origin`, `domain`, `range`, `scale`, `axisColor`, `labelColor`
- `FunctionPlot`: Plot a function on axes. Props: `fn` (function), `domain`, `origin`, `scale`, `color`
- `Vector`: Mathematical vector. Props: `from`, `to`, `color`, `label`
- `VectorField`: Grid of arrows. Props: `fn` (vector function), `domain`, `range`, `scale`
- `Matrix`: Matrix display with brackets. Props: `values` (2D array), `x`, `y`, `color`
- `Graph`: Graph theory visualization. Props: `nodes` (GraphNode[]), `edges` (GraphEdge[])
- `LaTeX`: LaTeX math expressions via KaTeX. Props: `expression`, `x`, `y`, `fontSize`, `color`, `align`
- `BarChart`: Animated bar chart. Props: `bars` (BarDef[]), `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`

### Motion
- Timeline tracks: animate document element properties with keyframes and easing.
- Reveal effects: progressively reveal content along a timeline.
- State machines: compose timeline states and interactive transitions.

### Presentations
- `Presentation`: Slide-deck system. Props: `width`, `height`, `background`, `transition` (`none`|`fade`|`slide-left`|`slide-up`|`zoom`), `transitionDuration`, `showHUD`, `showNotes`, `startSlide`
- `Slide`: Individual slide. Props: `title`, `notes`, `background`

## Hooks

- `useCurrentFrame()`: Returns current frame number (0-based)
- `interpolate(frame, inputRange, outputRange, options?)`: Map frames to values with easing
- `useElucimContext()`: Returns `{ frame, fps, durationInFrames, width, height }`
- `usePresentationContext()`: Returns `{ slideIndex, totalSlides, goTo, next, prev, isFullscreen, toggleFullscreen }`
- `useInsidePresentation()`: Returns boolean — true inside a Presentation

## Easing

Named: `linear`, `easeInQuad`, `easeOutQuad`, `easeInOutQuad`, `easeInCubic`, `easeOutCubic`, `easeInOutCubic`, `easeInQuart`, `easeOutQuart`, `easeInOutQuart`, `easeInSine`, `easeOutSine`, `easeInOutSine`, `easeInExpo`, `easeOutExpo`, `easeInOutExpo`, `easeInBack`, `easeOutBack`, `easeOutElastic`, `easeOutBounce`

Generators: `spring({ stiffness, damping, mass })`, `cubicBezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`

## DSL

The public DSL shape is the canonical `ElucimDocument`: `version: "2.0"`, a single `scene`, an ID-keyed `elements` registry, optional `timelines`, optional `stateMachines`, and optional `metadata`. Other document shapes are rejected.

Do not put `durationInFrames` on a document `scene`. Timelines, state machines, and explicit export policies own time.

```json
{
  "version": "2.0",
  "metadata": {
    "title": "Orbit reveal",
    "intent": "Explain a central orbit with a deterministic intro animation",
    "polishLevel": "draft"
  },
  "scene": {
    "type": "player",
    "width": 800,
    "height": 600,
    "fps": 30,
    "background": "#0d0d1a",
    "children": ["orbit"]
  },
  "elements": {
    "orbit": {
      "id": "orbit",
      "type": "circle",
      "role": "primary",
      "layout": { "x": 300, "y": 200, "width": 200, "height": 200 },
      "intent": { "importance": "primary", "generated": true },
      "props": {
        "type": "circle",
        "cx": 400,
        "cy": 300,
        "r": 80,
        "stroke": "$primary",
        "strokeWidth": 4,
        "fill": "none",
        "opacity": 0
      }
    }
  },
  "timelines": {
    "intro": {
      "id": "intro",
      "duration": 90,
      "tracks": [
        {
          "target": "orbit",
          "property": "opacity",
          "keyframes": [
            { "frame": 0, "value": 0 },
            { "frame": 20, "value": 1, "easing": "easeOutCubic" }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "defaultStateMachine": "main",
  "stateMachines": {
    "main": {
      "id": "main",
      "entry": "intro",
      "states": { "intro": { "timeline": "intro" } },
      "transitions": [{ "id": "entry-start", "from": "entry", "to": "intro", "trigger": "onStart" }]
    }
  }
}
```

Render with `<DslRenderer dsl={doc} />`. Validate with `validate(doc)` or `validateDocument(doc)`. Parse YAML with `fromYaml(yamlString)`. Math expressions in `functionPlot` props use safe evaluation (sin, cos, sqrt, etc.).

### Agent diagram polish

When generating Elucim diagrams, use the normalized `ElucimDocument` shape and run deterministic polish before returning the result.

- If working from a shell, use `npx @elucim/cli ops --json` to discover the CLI and code-backed agent operations. Then use `npx @elucim/cli validate`, `inspect`, `nudges`, `polish`, and `layout` to interrogate and improve documents without writing ad hoc scripts. Global installs expose the shorter `elucim` binary.
- Use `evaluateSceneForAgent(doc)` from `@elucim/dsl/agent`; inspect `report.layout`, `report.layoutRepairs`, and `report.polish` for text/layout issue codes, deterministic repair suggestions, category scores, and diagnostics. `report.valid` requires both schema validation and layout preflight to have no errors.
- Use `analyzePolish(doc)` from `@elucim/dsl` for direct polish analysis.
- Use `inspectPolishHeuristics(doc)` when you need the raw evidence behind the score: bounds, intersections, off-canvas overflow, text sizing, colors, graph crossings/overlaps, connector continuations, and semantic relationships.
- Use `suggestDocumentNudges(doc)` and `applyNudge(doc, nudge)` to make command-backed, previewable fixes.
- Apply `nudge.confidence === "safe"` nudges automatically. Treat `review` nudges as user/editor-review changes, especially graph layout.
- Use semantic roles and intent: `role: "title"`, `role: "callout"`, `intent.importance: "primary" | "secondary" | "supporting"`.
- Add explicit layout relationships when possible: `intent.target`, `intent.flowFrom`, `intent.flowTo`, `intent.relationship`, `intent.group`, plus `layout.rank` and `layout.locked`.
- Use semantic color tokens (`$title`, `$surface`, `$primary`, `$muted`) instead of many literal colors.
- Prefer agent-safe scene presets for text-heavy generated visuals: `createTextCalloutScenePreset()`, `createThreeCardFlowScenePreset()`, `createComparisonScenePreset()`, and `createAgentSafeDocument()` from `@elucim/dsl/agent`. These allocate bounded textboxes before validation/repair, and layout/text diagnostics count in the agent quality score.
- Prefer composite authoring helpers for designed-slide structure instead of hand-assembling loose primitives: `createStepCardPreset()`, `createTextBlockPreset()`, `createTextBoxPreset()`, `createCardGridPreset()`, `createConnectorPreset()`, `createDecisionNodePreset()`, `createBoundaryPreset()`, `createBadgePreset()`, `createQueueStackPreset()`, `createTimelineRoadmapPreset()`, `createComparisonTablePreset()`, `createAutoLayoutGroupPreset()`, and `createProgressiveRevealGroupPreset()` from `@elucim/dsl`.
- From the CLI, use `add-step-card`, `add-text-block`, `add-textbox`, `add-card-grid`, and `add-connector` to add those composites to an existing document. These write ordinary editable groups and primitives. Use `add-textbox` when generated copy must stay inside a known rectangle. `add-connector` supports `--line-style`, `--start-cap`, `--end-cap`, and `--stroke-width`.
- Use `createConnectorPreset()` or `elucim add-connector` for reading order and layout semantics. Generated connector intent contributes virtual ELK edges during semantic layout; the persisted document remains normal editable Elucim elements.
- Use semantic motion helpers for agent-authored animation intent instead of raw keyframes: `planMotionBeats()`, `createSemanticMotionTimeline()`, `createAutoStaggerTimeline()`, `createStateSnapshotMotion()`, `lintMotion()`, `previewBeatDiffs()`, `createReducedMotionDocument()`, and `holdFinalFrame()`.
- Semantic motion presets are `revealFlow`, `emphasizeDecision`, `tracePath`, `loopOnce`, `handoff`, `drainQueue`, and `compareBeforeAfter`. They compile to ordinary document timelines/state machines.
- From the CLI, use `add-beat`, `animate-flow`, `reveal-group`, `sample-beats`, `hold-final`, `reduced-motion`, and `export-frames` for beat-level motion workflows.
- Run `lintMotion()` or `elucim sample-beats` before returning animated diagrams. Check for blank first frames, too-fast transitions, simultaneous overload, hidden labels, flashing, excessive motion, static timelines, and missing reduced-motion fallbacks.
- For graph diagrams, provide stable node IDs and edges; the layered graph nudge can rewrite node `x`/`y` coordinates while preserving editability.
- Prefer helper presets such as `createCalloutCardPreset()` for explanatory callouts instead of assembling raw rectangles and text from scratch.
- For broader explanatory layouts, call `await suggestSemanticLayoutNudges(doc)` from `@elucim/dsl` and surface the returned ELK-backed `review` nudge instead of applying it silently.
- Surface the `smooth-connector-continuations` review nudge when straight connectors should read as smoother directional Bezier continuations.
- Hosts can call `getAgentOperationCatalog()` from `@elucim/dsl/agent` to pass agents the concrete authoring, validation, inspection, polish, and layout operations available in code.

### Agent authoring APIs

```typescript
import {
  createAgentSafeDocument,
  createTextCalloutScenePreset,
  validateForAgent,
} from '@elucim/dsl/agent';

const base = createAgentSafeDocument(createTextCalloutScenePreset({
  id: 'agent-draft',
  title: 'Hello Elucim',
  body: 'Generated copy lives inside bounded textboxes so it can be checked and repaired deterministically.',
  callout: 'Use raw text only for short labels or numbers.',
}), {
  metadata: { title: 'Agent draft', polishLevel: 'draft' },
});

const result = validateForAgent(base);
```
